default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-258.title: Hourly candle close-location carry
E-258.hypothesis: Desks and chart traders read hourly candles; an hour that was wider than usual and closed in its top (bottom) slice ends with buyers (sellers) still lifting at the bell, i.e. a parent order not finished. The faders who sold the hour's high are offside as the next hour opens, so follow the close side.

E-259.title: Low-volume micro-break fade
E-259.hypothesis: A close through the recent high/low printed on far less volume than usual for that minute was not pushed by informed size, only by a few small orders into a thin book; the liquidity providers who were run over re-quote and lean back, so fade the break.

E-260.title: Pre-New-York lull micro-break fade
E-260.hypothesis: Between the settled B3 open and the New York cash open, large index participants wait for US price discovery; breaks of the recent high/low in this window are local noise traded against market makers who are happy to provide liquidity, so they revert. Fade breaks only in the 9:30-10:25 lull.

E-261.title: Marginal-break fade
E-261.hypothesis: A close that clears the recent high/low by only a sliver triggers the breakout orders and the stops resting just beyond, but no buyer is paying up past them; once that small pool is filled there is nobody left on the break side and the resting liquidity pushes price back, so fade small breaks.

E-262.title: Stacked daily-extreme micro-break fade
E-262.hypothesis: Each of the last few sessions' highs and lows is a level where swing traders keep take-profit and fresh limit orders; a 15-minute break that runs into ANY of them (not only yesterday's or the channel edge) meets that resting supply/demand and stalls, so fade breaks that end near a stacked old extreme.

E-263.title: Indecisive-tape micro-break fade
E-263.hypothesis: When the recent bars are mostly small bodies inside their ranges, every bar is a two-way fight that the passive side wins; a break of the 15-minute extreme in such a tape is one more probe that the same passive traders absorb, so fade it.

E-264.title: Counter-drift micro-break fade
E-264.hypothesis: After a two-hour drift larger than usual, a 15-minute break against the drift is short covering or a dip-buyer's probe, while the participant behind the drift is still working the order; that order leans on the counter break, so fade it back toward the drift.

E-265.title: Spent volume-quota micro-break fade
E-265.hypothesis: Once the session has already traded most of a typical full day's volume, the day's big orders have been executed; later breaks of the recent high/low are not backed by fresh size and the participants who are done (and now take profit) meet them, so fade breaks after the volume quota is spent.

E-266.title: Flat-value micro-break fade
E-266.hypothesis: A session VWAP that has barely moved for half an hour means volume keeps trading at the same value on both sides: neither buyers nor sellers are moving value; a break of the recent high/low then trades away from accepted value and responsive traders return it, so fade breaks when value is flat.

E-267.title: Range-ahead-of-schedule micro-break fade
E-267.hypothesis: When today's range is already much wider than the usual range at this minute, day traders' targets are met early and the move is ahead of its normal schedule; new breaks then mostly carry late chasers who meet profit-takers, so fade breaks of the recent high/low on such days.
